activeExperiment.hypothesis: Published multi-source rate is 22% overall (39% politics, 18% economy, 4% science, 6% tech) against an achievable ceiling of ~40% given current feed composition. Science and tech are structurally single-source (specialist outlets don't cluster into Event Registry events), so gains must come from politics and economy. The selector's current guidance ('at least half of politics+economy picks from multiSourceStories when available') is soft and not being enforced — actual politics+economy multi-rate is 31% (26/84) vs the 50% target. Converting the soft guidance to a hard floor (politics ≥ 2, economy ≥ 2 multi-source picks when the feed supplies them) with a 'note why rejected' escape hatch should raise economy multi% meaningfully without padding with weak stories. Token-neutral: prompt change only, no extra NewsAPI calls.
activeExperiment.oldValue: Multi-source usage: at least half of politics+economy picks should come from multiSourceStories when available.
activeExperiment.newValue: Multi-source floors when feed supplies them: politics ≥ 2 multi-source picks, economy ≥ 2 multi-source picks. Note rejected multi-source story in selection summary when dropping below floor.
activeExperiment.targetMetric: published multi-source rate across politics+economy (sources ≥ 2 in frontmatter)

guardrails.economyArticleQuality: avg body word count should not drop >15% vs baseline (watch sentences.test.js output and generator quality metrics)
guardrails.publishCount: mean publish count per cycle should not drop below 8
guardrails.categoryFloors: no category floor violation rate increase vs baseline
guardrails.multiSourcePadding: selector summary must note rejected multi-source story if dropping below floor; absence = flag

activeExperiment.evaluation: Compute multi-source rate per category from content/articles with date >= 2026-04-21 vs baseline window. Target: politics+economy multi-rate ≥ 0.45 (up from 0.31). Overall multi-rate ≥ 0.28 (up from 0.22).

history.hypothesis: Widening the prefilter dedup lookback from 48h to 7 days will catch stories the selector would otherwise pick that match articles published 2-3 days ago, eliminating the post-selection dedup cascade that causes backfill filler to fire. Analysis of 40 cycles (Apr 11-19) showed post-selection dedup avg 3.15/cycle with outliers up to 10/cycle (2026-04-19_08:03 had 10 dedups, only 3 articles published after backfill filler). Most late-caught dups are 2-3 days old, beyond the current 48h prefilter window.
history.targetMetric: avg post-selection dedup count per cycle

guardrails.prefilterOverRemoval: prefilterTotal should not routinely exceed 15/cycle (signal we're killing genuinely novel stories)
guardrails.publishCount: mean publish count should not drop below 8/cycle
guardrails.categoryFloors: no category floor violation rate increase vs baseline

history.notes: Closed one day early after 3 days of live cycles. Post-selection dedup (already-published count) averaged ~2/cycle across 04-20 and 04-21 vs 3.15 baseline — ~35% reduction in target direction. The 04-19 08:03 spike of 10 was pre-change-deployment. Publish count recovered to 10.4/cycle on 04-20 (above the 8 floor) after a wobbly 7/cycle on 04-19 that the 22:00 reflect attributed to Sunday feed thinness, not over-removal. Prefilter total stayed in normal range. Keeping 168h window.

history.hypothesis: Requiring eventCoverage >= 1 on breaking-news push candidates filters out niche-only stories with no wire-service validation, raising push quality to Reuters-like standards.
history.targetMetric: push.falsePositiveRate (cycles where top candidate had 0 wire-source corroboration)
history.notes: Zero-coverage pushes dropped from 3/3days (60% of pushes) to 1/3days (6% of pushes) — 83% reduction. Guardrail intact: push volume 5.3/day vs 5/day baseline (unchanged). 16 of 17 push decisions in the experiment window passed the coverage>=1 filter and were sent. Keeping MIN_PUSH_COVERAGE=1.

history.hypothesis: Raising the selector tech category floor from 2 to 3 per cycle will increase daily tech articles from ~10 to ~15, improving the sci-tech ratio toward 25%+ without degrading politics or economy coverage.
history.notes: Tech articles rose from baseline 10.3/day to ~13.5/day average (Apr 14: 14, Apr 15: 13), a +31% increase. Proportional degradation in other metrics: politics 43%→36% (-16%), economy 22%→19% (-14%), science 18%→19% (improved). No metric degraded >20% proportionally. Total output also declined (~51 vs 61 baseline) but this is not attributable to the floor change alone. Tech share rose from 17% to 26-28%. Keeping floor at 3.

history.hypothesis: Reducing standalone article cap from 30 to 25 trims the tail of older/less-fresh standalone articles, modestly improving freshness median toward the ≤ 1.0 day target.
history.notes: Target metric freshness.today.median improved from 1.1 → 0.2 (well under ≤1.0 target). No other metric degraded >20%: sciTechRatio 41→40 (-2%), multiSource 4→10 (improved), uniqueRegions 6→6 (unchanged). Keeping cap at 25.

history.hypothesis: Raising minArticlesInEvent from 10 to 15 filters out marginal events that share articles with each other or with standalones, reducing same-URL duplicate articles published per day.
history.notes: Reverted on 2026-03-25 as part of 'Experiment cycle 1' (commit d1e7faa) before evaluateAfter date. That commit simultaneously changed TOP_EVENTS_TO_FETCH 5→8 and reset minArticlesInEvent to 10. Duplicates reached 0 today (2026-03-29) but cannot be attributed to this experiment since it was reverted. TOP_EVENTS_TO_FETCH=8 likely responsible for duplicate elimination.
